summary: Deferred warmup bug leads to intermittent GPU assignments and 40% dedicated-pool throughput drop
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Acero Labs reported a sudden throughput degradation in their dedicated pool in prod-us-west starting 2026-03-13 09:10 UTC. P50 throughput dropped ~40% over a 30-minute window; p95 latency increased ~2x for short/interactive routes. The customer observed frequent short-lived failures and fallback routing to lower-tier models.

Impact:
- Dedicated pool for Acero Labs (reserved capacity) saw sustained throughput degradation on interactive routes (text-generation chat).
- Customers experienced elevated latencies and increased fallback to hosted models, causing increased cost and degraded SLA adherence.
- A subset of requests returned 503/504 during the window as GPU attachments lagged.

Environment:
- prod-us-west (us-west-2 region)
- Dedicated pool: reserved-ACERO-01 (8-GPU A100 equivalent)
- Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream and some short-text generation API routes

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send 80 concurrent short-stream requests (avg token length ~80) pinned to reserved-ACERO-01.
2) Observe that some requests queue while other requests start and complete; GPU slot utilization shows oscillation.
3) Re-run after ~5 minutes: behavior can be intermittent (sometimes normal).

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler did not trigger expected warmup pre-attach behavior for bursty short streams, leading to frequent late GPU attachments and transient slot shortages.
- Several ephemeral tenants generated short bursts that caused eviction loops and increased device churn.
- Telemetry showed heartbeats from the serving-sidecar were sometimes tagged with stale instance IDs, causing the scheduler to consider those sessions cold.

Expected behavior:
- Warmup pre-attachment should detect burst patterns and pre-attach spare slots; autoscaler should scale proactively and avoid 503s and late attachments.

Initial logs/links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/throughput/dedicated-pool?orgId=1&var-pool=reserved-ACERO-01&from=2026-03-13T09:00:00Z&to=2026-03-13T10:00:00Z
- Traces: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/7ac2f4a8-9e2b-11ec-9f91-0a58ac140005
- Sidecar PR that rolled 2026-03-13 morning: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar/pull/1823

Customer contact:
- Primary: support@acerolabs.ai (Victor Chen)
comments: 2026-03-13 09:25 - Support (Maya Patel): Acknowledged with customer, opened investigation and escalated to SRE. Escalation note: suspected warmup/autoscaler misclassification.

2026-03-13 09:40 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Observed GPU attach latency spikes on reserved-ACERO-01; slot churn correlates with short-lived streams. Seeing sidecar heartbeats with duplicate instance tags in telemetry. Pulling sidecar rollout audit.

2026-03-13 10:05 - Eng (Priya Singh): Sidecar PR 1823 added instance-id normalization; rollback recommended as rollback prevents aggregation bug. Opening PR to revert. Linking autoscaler metrics for correlation.

2026-03-13 10:30 - Support (Maya Patel): Shared workaround with customer: temporarily increase dedicated pool min-capacity by +2 GPU-equivalents and enable slot-pin on critical routes. Customer applied; reported partial improvement.

2026-03-13 11:15 - Customer (Victor Chen, Acero Labs): Noted improvement after temporary capacity bump; still seeing intermittent 503s on cold-starts for short streams. Asked for ETA on permanent fix.

2026-03-14 02:10 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Rolled back sidecar change in staging and validated heartbeat tags normalized. Scheduling production rollback during low-traffic window 03:00 UTC. Monitoring post-rollback telemetry.

2026-03-14 04:00 - Support (Maya Patel): Production rollback completed. Early metrics show slot churn reduced and throughput returning to baseline for Acero Labs. Notifying customer and keeping ticket open for 24-48h observation.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- 09:05 UTC: Deployment of sidecar PR 1823 began in us-west canary pool; change introduced instance-id normalization but accidentally left a fallback path that emitted stale IDs for short-lived streams.
- 09:15-09:40 UTC: Scheduler telemetry shows an increase in 'cold' classification events for active sessions. Autoscaler warmup windows rely on heartbeat continuity; mis-tagging led to deferred warmup and failure to pre-attach.
- 09:30 UTC: Multiple ephemeral tenants produced many small short-lived streams; without warmup these caused repeated attach/detach and eviction loops (noisy-neighbor amplification).
- Correlated metrics: attach_latency_p50 spiked from ~80ms to ~900ms; attach_failure_rate rose to 6%; throughput (tokens/s) dropped ~40%.
- Hypothesis: Sidecar heartbeat tagging bug caused the scheduler to ignore recent activity, so autoscaler heuristics treated demand as new/cold and deferred warmup until after the first few requests hit. This allowed short bursts to consume slots inefficiently and triggered eviction and prefetch churn.
- Reproduce: Canary rollback + synthetic short-stream flood reliably reproduces throughput drop versus baseline.
- Temporary mitigations tested: 1) Manual min-capacity bump, 2) Route-level slot-pin to reserved GPUs, 3) Short-term increase to autoscaler aggressiveness. All reduce 503s but do not address root cause.
resolution_notes:
Actions taken:
- 2026-03-14 03:00 UTC: Rolled back sidecar PR 1823 in us-west and restarted sidecar on affected hosts.
- 2026-03-14 03:30 UTC: Observed normalization of heartbeat tags and immediate reduction in cold-classification events.
- 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC: Reduced manual capacity bump back to baseline after 1 hour of stable metrics; customer confirmed throughput recovered within 20 minutes.
- Created follow-up tasks: (1) Fix sidecar instance-id fallback and add unit/integration tests, (2) Add telemetry alert that fires when heartbeat tag variance increases >10% vs baseline, (3) Add autoscaler safety guard to avoid deferring warmup for short-burst patterns for dedicated pools.
- Communications: Notified customer (Victor Chen) of rollback and ongoing remediation plan. Preparing postmortem doc and RCA for Confluence.
resolution: Mitigated - permanent fix in progress (rolled back faulty sidecar change). Monitoring and follow-up tickets created.
next_steps: 1) Complete sidecar fix and deploy with canary tests (owner: sidecar team, due: 2026-03-18). 2) Implement heartbeat-variance alert (owner: telemetry, due: 2026-03-16). 3) Autoscaler guard PR to be prioritized (owner: autoscaler team, due: 2026-03-20). 4) Customer follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-15 15:00 PDT.
